rubric.item: SPEC-17 correctness (no src/ui or src/advice changes)

findings.issue: No test plays an exact-stack all-in call through to the end of the hand and asserts that nothing is returned (`result.returned` absent) and that the award equals the full pot. The `exactCall` case checks only `allIn` and `toAct`. The tie-at-top branch of gather is pinned by older showdown tests, but none of them involve an all-in seat.
findings.evidence: exactCall = apply(facing(8), [3,'call',4]); expect(allInOf(exactCall,3)).toBe(true); expect(exactCall.toAct).toBe(1) -- the hand is not continued. I ran a 60,000-hand random short-stack fuzz (checkStep on every action, chip conservation, award+returned = total put in, allIn <=> stack 0 mid-hand, toAct never all-in/folded): 0 violations, which included exact-match all-ins. So the behaviour is correct; this is a gap in the tests only.
findings.fix: Continue exactCall to showdown (seat 1 calls 4, then turn/river checked by 2 and 1) and assert `result.returned` is undefined, the award equals the sum of totalContribution, and checkState is [].

findings.issue: In C4, the local `backed` (chips returned to this seat) reads like a past-tense verb.

summary: The engine change matches the spec. Changes checked: call = min(owe, stack); allIn set when a call, bet or raise leaves stack 0; all-in seats skipped in round-closing and in toAct, both mid-street and at the first actor on a new street; the D-7 runout through the dealNextStreet helper from preflop, flop or turn; the uncalled return in gather only when exactly one seat holds the top street contribution, so ties return nothing. Chip conservation holds in every case checked. That covers the exact-match all-in, the partly uncalled all-in bet (S-C), the bet a folded seat raised over (folded contributions are counted, per A-5) and returns in fold-outs. In theory the round-continue path could drop gathered.returned, but that path always has two or more open seats at currentBet, so back is 0 there. The checker has C3/C4 net of returned. C5 uses an independent formula based on total contributions and runs only in checkStep, when no chips violation was already found. Independent checks: a random fuzz of 60,000 hands with 3-7 seats and stacks of $5-$44 or $160 found 0 violations, not counting the expected bet-cap ones (no cap until TASK-1.12). It hit 23.7k hands with an all-in, 45.8k returns and 14.6k runouts (4.6k from preflop). The 10,000-hand playtest output is byte-identical to the baseline. The vitest engine/table/playtest/ui suites passed (187 tests), and the e2e next-hand and review specs passed in both browsers (12 tests). Locked edits E1-E8 change only the listed amounts and messages; E1 also adds the `returned` key. Nothing was removed or loosened. U1-U4 match the spec. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings; one MINOR test gap and one NIT.
